title: Accessibility Standard: Accommodation Review Days for Video Hearings, Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
A medical statement exhibit received on the appeal is what gives a video hearing session of Unemployment Insurance Appeals its *video accommodation review days*, which depend on whether at least one medical statement exhibit stands received on the appeal and on the latest interpreter request on the appeal.

**Standard.** The video accommodation review days are the sign-language review days when the latest interpreter request on the appeal is for American Sign Language and at least one medical statement exhibit stands received on the appeal, the medical-letter review days when at least one medical statement exhibit stands received on the appeal and the latest interpreter request is not for American Sign Language or no interpreter is requested, and zero days when no medical statement exhibit stands received on the appeal. These days are added to the video block gap, and the set hearing date is moved later by the total before the calendar-day rule is applied.

| Medical statement exhibit received on the appeal | Latest interpreter request | Accommodation review days |
|---|---|---|
| at least one | American Sign Language | 5 (sign-language review) |
| at least one | any other language, Spanish included | 3 (medical-letter review) |
| at least one | none requested | 3 (medical-letter review) |
| none | any, or none | 0 |

## Points of judgement

- A medical statement exhibit is an exhibit of the kind *medical statement* recorded as received on this appeal, from any party.
- Without a medical statement exhibit there are no review days, even where the latest interpreter request is for American Sign Language.
- "Latest" means the interpreter request with the most recent request date on the appeal.

*Hypothetical cases:* (1) one medical statement received; requests were American Sign Language, then Spanish — the latest is Spanish, so 3 days. (2) two medical statements received; the only request is American Sign Language — 5 days. (3) no medical statement; the latest request is American Sign Language — 0 days.
